description: Design a cache memory system with a simple Least Recently Used (LRU) replacement policy. The cache should have a fixed number of lines (e.g., 4 lines) and a way to track the usage of each line. Implement a module that accepts memory addresses for read and write operations, and replaces the least recently used line when a cache miss occurs.
code:
module cache_lru (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [7:0] address, // 8-bit address input
    input wire read,          // read operation
    input wire write,         // write operation
    output reg hit,           // cache hit
    output reg [7:0] data_out // data output
);
    reg [7:0] cache [3:0];     // 4 lines of cache
    reg [1:0] lru_counter [3:0]; // Counter for LRU tracking
    reg [1:0] next_lru;        // Next line to replace
    integer i;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                cache[i] <= 8'b0;
                lru_counter[i] <= 2'b0;
            end
            hit <= 0;
            data_out <= 8'b0;
        end else begin
            hit <= 0;
            for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                if (cache[i] == address) begin
                    hit <= 1;
                    data_out <= cache[i]; // return data
                    lru_counter[i] <= 2'b00; // Reset the LRU counter
                end else begin
                    lru_counter[i] <= lru_counter[i] + 1; // Increment other counters
                end
            end

            if (write && !hit) begin
                // Find the least recently used line
                next_lru = 0;
                for (i = 1; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                    if (lru_counter[i] > lru_counter[next_lru]) begin
                        next_lru = i;
                    end
                end
                cache[next_lru] <= address; // Replace the LRU line
                lru_counter[next_lru] <= 2'b00; // Reset LRU counter
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

    output reg expired
);

    input clk,  
    input reset,  
    input data_in,  
    input ack_nack,

);

                end  
            endcase  
        end  
    end

    input [0:8*3*3-1] weight_matrix, // 3x3 matrix packed into a single input
    output reg [0:8*3*3-1] shortest_paths  // 3x3 matrix packed into a single output
);

    end

Design a DVFS (Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling) controller in Verilog that adjusts voltage and frequency based on a temperature input. If the temperature exceeds a threshold (e.g., 75°C), the circuit should lower the frequency and voltage; if the temperature is below 50°C, it should increase them. The controller should have three states: HIGH, MEDIUM, and LOW, represented by a 2-bit state variable. The output should represent the current frequency and voltage settings.
code:
module DVFS_Controller(
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [7:0] temperature, // 8-bit temperature input
    output reg [1:0] state, // 2-bit state output
    output reg [1:0] voltage, // 2-bit voltage level
    output reg [1:0] frequency // 2-bit frequency level
);
    // State encoding
    localparam HIGH = 2'b00;
    localparam MEDIUM = 2'b01;
    localparam LOW = 2'b10;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= MEDIUM; // Default state
            voltage <= 2'b10; // Default high voltage
            frequency <= 2'b10; // Default high frequency
        end else begin
            case (state)
                HIGH: begin
                    if (temperature > 75) begin
                        state <= MEDIUM;
                        voltage <= 2'b01; // Lower voltage
                        frequency <= 2'b01; // Lower frequency
                    end
                end
                MEDIUM: begin
                    if (temperature > 75) begin
                        state <= LOW;
                        voltage <= 2'b00; // Lowest voltage
                        frequency <= 2'b00; // Lowest frequency
                    end else if (temperature < 50) begin
                        state <= HIGH;
                        voltage <= 2'b10; // High voltage
                        frequency <= 2'b10; // High frequency
                    end
                end
                LOW: begin
                    if (temperature < 50) begin
                        state <= MEDIUM;
                        voltage <= 2'b01; // Medium voltage
                        frequency <= 2'b01; // Medium frequency
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

    input wire rst,
    input wire [3:0] data_in,

);

reg [2:0] count; // 3 bits to count 0-7

);

The module should have inputs for the data to be transmitted, a send signal, and a clock. The output should be the serial data being transmitted. code:
module uart_transmitter (
    input wire clk,       // Clock signal
    input wire send,      // Signal to send data
    input wire [7:0] data, // 8-bit data input
    output reg tx        // Transmit output
);
    reg [3:0] state;     // State of the FSM
    reg [3:0] bit_index; // Current bit index
    reg [11:0] baud_count; // Baud rate counter

    parameter IDLE = 4'b0000, START_BIT = 4'b0001, DATA_BITS = 4'b0010, STOP_BIT = 4'b0011;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        case (state)
            IDLE: begin
                tx <= 1; // Idle state, tx high
                if (send) begin
                    state <= START_BIT; // Move to start bit
                    bit_index <= 0; // Reset bit index
                    baud_count <= 0; // Reset baud count
                end
            end
            
            START_BIT: begin
                tx <= 0; // Start bit is low
                if (baud_count == 10416) begin // Wait for one bit duration (1 MHz clock for 9600 baud)
                    baud_count <= 0; // Reset baud count
                    state <= DATA_BITS; // Move to data bits
                end else begin
                    baud_count <= baud_count + 1; 
                end
            end
            
            DATA_BITS: begin
                tx <= data[bit_index]; // Transmit data bit
                if (baud_count == 10416) begin // Wait for one bit duration
                    baud_count <= 0; // Reset baud count
                    if (bit_index == 7) begin
                        state <= STOP_BIT; // Move to stop bit
                    end else begin
                        bit_index <= bit_index + 1; // Move to next bit
                    end
                end else begin
                    baud_count <= baud_count + 1; 
                end
            end

            STOP_BIT: begin
                tx <= 1; // Stop bit is high
                if (baud_count == 10416) begin // Wait for one bit duration
                    baud_count <= 0; // Reset baud count
                    state <= IDLE; // Back to idle
                end else begin
                    baud_count <= baud_count + 1; 
                end
            end

            default: state <= IDLE; // Default state
        endcase
    end
endmodule

        if (last_signal > 0 && signal_in <= 0) begin
